text:
sasha: Heads-up — AtlasPay (enterprise) just pushed a firm ask: 95th percentile latency <150ms at sustained 2k qps for text-gen (hosted tier). They want a contractual SLA or we route them to Dedicated. Can we RICE this vs the cost-optimization work (quantization recommendations + batching heuristics)?

mike: wow that's tight. do we know model size/profile? CPU vs GPU?

sasha: they’re on a 1.3B-ish open model variant today, mostly short prompts (avg 60 tokens). prefer hosted but willing to pay for dedicated if we can guarantee it.

jordan: my first take — this is very high reach (enterprise revenue), high impact for Sales. But effort might be 8-12 pwk to build routing + SLO enforcement + perf testing infra.

ria: quick RICE sketch (rough):
```
Reach = enterprise ARR / platform users -> high (score 9)
Impact = 3 (merchant-critical but niche)
Confidence = 0.6
Effort = 10 person-weeks
Score = (9 * 3 * 0.6) / 10 = 1.62
```

ow compare to cost-optimize work (quant recs + batching):
```
Reach = broad (all customers) -> 8
Impact = 2 (unit cost savings)
Confidence = 0.8
Effort = 6 pwk
Score = (8 * 2 * 0.8) / 6 = 2.13
```

ria: so baseline says cost-opt wins on pure RICE. but feels off because enterprise revenue is underweighted here.

ow product-bot: @sasha added a link: https://redwood.internal/sheets/atlaspay-sla (access restricted) :link:

owen: agree with Ria — RICE as-is misses strategic value + churn risk. what if we reweight reach for enterprise deals or add a strategic multiplier?

sasha: exactly — I propose we run a quick sensitivity: two RICE runs: (A) vanilla (current weights) (B) enterprise-weighted where Reach*1.7 for named accounts, Confidence bumped +0.1 because Sales validated demand.

mike: also need to account for sequencing cost: we could ship a lighter MVP (routing + prioritization rules, soft SLO) in 4 wks, then hard SLO + dedicated pool in 8 more. split effort reduces risk and unlocks revenue earlier.

jordan: propose acceptance criteria for MVP:
- canary route AtlasPay traffic to a reserved pool
- automated alert if 95th > 200ms for 10m window
- rollout docs + billing flag

ria: and for full SLA rollout:
- reproducible perf tests at 2k qps with synthetic load
- capacity autoscaler rules + failover to compatible model variant
- accounting for cost uplift in pricing

sasha: Sales wants a yes/no in 48h on whether we do spike and prioritization. Recommend: 3-day spike to validate perf with synthetic load + quick estimate of engineering work. If spike looks good, we re-run RICE with enterprise weighting and move to MVP planning.

owen: +1. Who owns spike? eng-runtime + perf. I can pair with Jordan.

mike: I'll draft the updated RICE sheet (two scenarios) and add sequencing lanes (mvp -> full).

jordan: if we go this route, add QA perf gate and a canary-only billing waiver so Sales can pilot without committing full discount.

sasha: decision for now: run 3-day perf spike (owner: owen/jordan). mike to publish dual RICE variants by EOD. we’ll reconvene after spike. :thumbsup:

product-bot: Created card PROD-4982 "AtlasPay SLA spike" and assigned to owen, jordan, mike. Due: 3 days.

mike: noted, will push RICE table to the sheet and ping channel when done.

ria: one more ask — add confidence notes in the sheet explaining assumptions (model size, avg tokens, tail behavior). those drive big differences.

sasha: thanks all. if spike fails, fallback is to offer Dedicated or adjusted pricing. if spike passes, we still need rollout guardrails (canary + auto-fallback).

owen: starting perf harness tomorrow morning. will post logs/initial numbers in this thread.

mike: thanks — big win if we can convert AtlasPay.

jordan: short term: reweighting RICE for GTM-sensitive requests is a pattern we should formalize. adding a field "strategic_multiplier" sounds useful.

sasha: agreed — capture that as an agenda item for next biz-prio sync.

product-bot: thread closed (auto) — reminder: check PROD-4982 status in 72h.
